description: A PHP static analysis tool for finding errors and security vulnerabilities in PHP applications

latest_release.body:
<!-- Release notes generated using configuration in .github/release.yml at 2d8a48d1611508108eaa653ef599010da65eff3f -->

## What's Changed
### Features
* Array offsets: Report a `false` offset, which PHP turns into `0` by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12690
* CLI: Add `--min-type-coverage` to fail below a type coverage minimum by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14075
* Language server: Apply the baseline as the CLI does by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13775
### Fixes
* Docblock types: Recognize `non-empty-scalar` and similar types in namespaces by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14079
* Docblock types: `empty-scalar` and `non-empty-scalar` no longer accept any scalar by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14080
* Language server: Reject unrecognised short options by @jay23606 in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13763
* Loops: Report definite issues of a `do-while`'s first iteration, not `Possibly*` by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14032
* Loops: Report an argument issue once, not once per loop pass by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14103
* Loops: Propagate types through nested `foreach` and references by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14099
* Mixed: Keep a `mixed` variable `mixed` after an `if` that wrote its offsets by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14039
* Mixed: Keep a `mixed` variable `mixed` after `else`, `switch`, `match` and `||` by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14063
* Mixed: Fix false `PossiblyUndefinedVariable` after `isset($var[$k])` by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14065
* Mixed: Fix false `InvalidArrayOffset` on nested writes by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14062
* Named arguments: Report the right argument number by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14096
* Narrowing: Narrow impossible `null` comparisons to `never` by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14036
* Narrowing: Narrow exhaustive `instanceof` checks to `never` by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14048
* Narrowing: Fix false contradictions on `===` between overlapping types by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14037
* Narrowing: `class_exists()` narrows only inside its `if` block by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13391
* Narrowing: `$a?->m() ?? false` narrows `$a` to non-null by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12995
* Narrowing: Narrow variables bound by reference in conditions by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14101
* Property hooks: Fix `__METHOD__` and false `LessSpecificReturnType` by @danog in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14066
* PHP 8.6: Allow `#[\Override]` on class constants and enum cases by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14038
* Plugins: Resolve class names in all type declarations of the AST by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14134
* Properties: Forget property items a called method writes by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14027
* Purity: Account for implicit `__toString()` calls by @shu-chen-dot-ca in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13782
* Stubs: `filter_var(null)` returns `''` by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14124
* Stubs: `libxml_set_external_entity_loader()` is not an unused call by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14118
* Stubs: `pathinfo()` may omit `dirname` by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14122
* Stubs: Fix write-only by-reference params of `proc_open()` and others by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14100
* Stubs: Fix `SplObjectStorage` value checks and param names by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14121
* Stubs: `stream_get_meta_data()` keys may be undefined by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/14095
* Templates: Narrow `key-of<T>`/`value-of<T>` instead of reporting contradictio

detail.readme:
Psalm

[![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/v/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/dt/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm coverage](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/coverage.svg?)](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm level](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/level.svg?)](https://psalm.dev/) Psalm is a static analysis tool for finding errors in PHP applications. [Join the official Psalm news channel](https://t.me/psalmphp) and the Psalm community on [Telegram](https://t.me/psalmphp_community) and [Discord](https://discord.gg/RwH8rEpxt9)! ## Installation To get started, check out the [installation guide](docs/running_psalm/installation.md). ## Live Demo You can play around with Psalm [on its website](https://psalm.dev/). ## Documentation Documentation is available on [Psalm’s website](https://psalm.dev/docs), generated from the [docs](https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/blob/master/docs) folder. ## Support Psalm development You can support Psalm development by requesting a support contract from [Daniil Gentili](https://daniil.it), the only active maintainer of Psalm. Support contracts can cover full integration of Psalm into existing codebases, support for Psalm issues and development of additional Psalm features. See [here »](https://daniil.it) for info, pricing and contact information. ## Interested in contributing? Have a look at [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Who made this Built by Matt Brown ([@muglug](https://github.com/muglug)). Maintained by Daniil Gentili ([@danog](https://github.com/danog)), Alies Lapatsin ([@alies-dev](https://github.com/alies-dev)) and Orklah ([@orklah](https://github.com/orklah)). Former maintainer: Bruce Weirdan ([@weirdan](https://github.com/weirdan)). The engineering team at [Vimeo](https://github.com/vimeo) have provided a lot encouragement, especially [@nbeliard](https://github.com/nbeliard), [@erunion](https://github.com/erunion) and [@nickyr](https://github.com/nickyr).
